results.diagnosis: The add function is using subtraction (a - b) instead of addition (a + b).
The function fails to divide the discount_percent by 100 to convert it from a percentage to a decimal multiplier before calculating the discount amount.
The comparison operator should be >= (greater than or equal to) instead of > (greater than) to allow a score of exactly 60 to pass.
The function reverses the entire string character by character instead of reversing the order of words.
The function uses range(n) which generates 0 to n-1, but it should generate 1 to n inclusive to correctly sum all numbers up to and including n.
Mutable default argument causes the same list object to be reused across function calls, leading to values from previous calls persisting in the list.
The count_words function treats words as case-sensitive, but the test expects case-insensitive counting; the function must convert words to lowercase before counting.
The factorial function's base case only checks for n == 1, missing the mathematical definition that factorial(0) should return 1, causing infinite recursion when n=0.
The function does not handle division by zero, causing a ZeroDivisionError instead of returning 0.
The function doesn't handle invalid inputs (None or non-numeric strings), causing ValueError and TypeError exceptions instead of returning 0.
The function uses an off-by-one index error by accessing items[len(items)] instead of items[len(items) - 1], and doesn't handle the empty list case to return None.
The function directly accesses a dictionary key that may not exist, causing a KeyError instead of returning None when the "email" key is missing.
The function uses the union operator (|) instead of the intersection operator (&), returning all elements from both lists instead of only the common elements.
The function converts to lowercase but forgets to strip leading and trailing whitespace.
The base case only checks for n == 1, but factorial(0) should also return 1; the condition should be n <= 1 or n == 0 to handle the zero case.
The while loop condition uses 'low < high' instead of 'low <= high', causing it to exit prematurely without checking the element at the final position when low equals high.
The function crashes with a ZeroDivisionError when given an empty list because it divides by len(numbers) without checking if the list is empty first.
The function doesn't convert the input text to lowercase, so uppercase or mixed-case buzzwords like "Passionate" or "NINJA" fail to match their lowercase counterparts in the BUZZWORDS list.
